title: The Half-Paid Term
summary: Sunrise Primary's fee spreadsheet says the term is almost fully paid. The school account says otherwise. Find out who still owes, and why the sheet is wrong.

client.name: Mrs. Adaeze Chukwu
brief: Our bursary clerk's sheet says almost every family has paid in full for the term. But the account balance tells a different story.
Parents pay in bits — part cash, part transfer — and some bank transfers bounce days later. I need to know exactly who still owes, and how much, before half-term reports go out.
client.thanks: Now I can see it in black and white. I'll call the parents on this list myself. Thank you, cadet.

starterSql:
-- Sunrise Primary: who still owes fees this term?
-- students: one row per pupil, with the term fee for their class.
-- payments: every payment logged against a student — some are partial, some bounced or were entered twice.

SELECT *
FROM payments
LIMIT 20;

tables.name: students
tables.description: Every pupil enrolled this term, with the fee owed for their class.

columns.name: term_fee
columns.desc: Full term fee for their class, in naira (₦)

tables.name: payments
tables.description: Every payment logged against a student this term. Parents often pay in two or three instalments.

columns.name: status
columns.desc: confirmed, reversed (bank bounced it) or duplicate (entered twice by mistake)

hints.title: Hint 1: Only confirmed money counts
hints.desc: A reversed payment bounced — the money never arrived. A duplicate is the same payment typed in twice. Neither should count toward what a family has paid.

hints.title: Hint 2: Join and sum per pupil
hints.desc: Join students to payments, keep only status = 'confirmed', and total each pupil's confirmed payments.
hints.snippet: LEFT JOIN payments p ON p.student_id = s.student_id

hints.title: Hint 3: Shape of the answer
hints.desc: One row per pupil who still owes money: their name and term_fee minus confirmed payments. Leave out anyone who has paid in full.

findings.claim: How much does Sunrise Primary still have outstanding this term, and from how many pupils?

options.text: ₦158,500 from 11 pupils — every logged payment counted, reversed and duplicate included
₦201,500 from 13 pupils — only confirmed payments counted
Nothing — the fee sheet is correct and every family has paid in full

findings.claim: Why does the clerk's spreadsheet look so much better than the real picture?

options.text: It counts bounced bank transfers and duplicate entries as if the money had actually arrived.
The school is quietly giving every family a discount.
The clerk is looking at last term's payments by mistake.

successFeedback: Once bounced transfers and double-entered payments are taken out, thirteen families are still short — ₦201,500 in all. The clerk was simply counting money that never arrived.

fixtures.purpose: A class where most payments bounced or were duplicated
fixtures.failHint: A reversed or duplicate payment never actually arrived — don't count it toward what a pupil has paid.

fixtures.purpose: A term where every pupil has paid in full
fixtures.failHint: When nobody still owes money, your query should return no rows.

evidence.title: A bank reversal notice
evidence.text: Pinned to the bursary noticeboard: "NOTICE OF REVERSAL — transfer reference TRX-88213 for ₦12,500 was returned unpaid (insufficient funds) three days after it was logged as received. Please update the ledger." Underneath, in pen: "Also check for anyone who got entered twice — Kemi's assistant typed Femi's payment in twice last week."
